Hi everyone! My name is Ray (GitHub: ray-shang); I'm an algebraic geometry PhD at Cambridge. I have finished formalizing the category algebra for an R-linear category, along with its universal property. This is building off of the work of Bernhard in #Is there code for X? > Path algebra of a quiver (I obtained his permission).

I would love to contribute this to Mathlib.

Update: The current WIP PR is here: - #42831 feat(CategoryTheory/Linear): category algebra of R-linear category
Hi Ray, you don't need write access to mathlib4 to open a PR. https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/index.html has more information about this.
(actually I might have posted the wrong guide...)
Ah actually, the nested guide has direct information about this https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/how-to-contribute.html
@Ray Shang for our education, could you please tell us how you concluded that you needed to ask for write access here?

Hi, I'm sorry for my confusion and thanks for your help. I don't really know what write access means; I treat a lot of these things as black boxes. I've been lurking on this zulip for a while and sometimes would scroll around the new members section for fun. I think I must have gotten the impression to ask for write access because of a zulip chat I read. So in the guide https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/how-to-contribute.html where it says to introduce yourself, I thought these would be the right words to say to get started. I realize now it doesn't mention anything about write access, but since it didn't, maybe I thought I should be safer than sorry (i.e. confused later on) and asked anyway, since 'write access' seemed like a reasonable sounding thing...

For context: Most open source projects use a system where people looking to make contributions fork the repository on github, do work there and open a PR from their repo. So e.g. if the open source project is called "Foo", then a contributor would open a PR requesting to merge yourname/master into foo/master.

However, for a long time, Mathlib's GitHub actions did not work properly outside of the repo. This meant that if you forked the mathlib4 repository, it caused a bunch of technical difficulties. So the standard solution was that anyone looking to contribute to mathlib first request write access to non-master branches of mathlib4. This means that instead of forking mathlib4, contributors directly committed to the mathlib4 repo on a non-master branch and then opened a pull request from mathlib4/newfeature to mathlib4/master.

Eventually, the people managing mathlib's CI did a bunch of engineering to make it work with forks properly. So mathlib has now gone back to the standard open source system where people fork the repository on github and open a PR from their repo. No one needs to request write access anymore. Ruben was asking where you read that you needed write access because if you read it on the website or official documentation then that means we need to update that documentation.
